decision: Retain the current blocking token stage. HIP API tracing shows the target wall/device-union difference is dominated by required queue dependencies inside blocking copies, not removable host idle. A default-off async root-token H2D removes one blocking call per cycle but does not improve complete wall and is removed.

conclusion: Blocking hipMemcpy API wall includes waiting for prior default-stream target kernels; its ~97-109 ms D2H calls are producer dependencies, not transfer overhead available for deletion.

The residual wall-minus-union also includes sequential API submission and host work; kernel launch API totals ~20.3 ms over 3,148 launches, but already-screened graph capture and broad launch coarsening are non-viable.
